retained_skill: Tune an SVD collaborative-filtering model to satisfy a held-out RMSE target while controlling the factor-model size.
bottleneck: All measured attempts first lose time installing and reconciling Python environments before repeatedly rewriting complete training scripts; 11 of 12 then use pandas plus Dataset.load_from_df, whose integer raw IDs the seed verifier unfairly evaluates with string IDs and reports as unknown-user predictions. Ten attempts exhaust the time budget, while attempt-08 locally reaches RMSE 0.913968 and 2.72 MB but is graded at RMSE 1.1303.
change: Repair the verifier to evaluate the stated prediction behavior independent of whether CSV IDs entered Surprise as integers or strings. Add an environment-supplied starter training script that handles dependency resolution, CSV loading, the stated split, evaluation, and serialization, leaving its deliberately inadequate SVD configuration for the student to tune. This structural help is in the original workspace signal: the student runs and edits the training program, observes its RMSE and size, and still decides how to tune SVD. It removes the package-installation and whole-script-rewrite stage (typically turns 2 through 18, plus later rewrites) rather than adding a document to read.
restore: A later hardening can remove the starter script and its two-sentence instruction passage, returning dependency setup, data loading, evaluation, and serialization to the student while leaving the SVD tuning contract unchanged.
prediction: The change addresses installing pip/packages and recreating the complete pipeline before tuning. With those mechanics prepared, attempts can immediately run a baseline, vary SVD configuration, and save a loadable model; ID normalization then lets the grader recognize the same held-out quality they measured locally. This is refuted if attempts use the starter yet still spend most turns on setup, or if a locally qualifying starter-produced model still fails grader RMSE.
